name: Hermansky-Pudlak Syndrome due to BLOC-2 Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of oculocutaneous albinism with hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and eyes
Platelet storage pool deficiency demonstrated by absent or reduced dense granules on electron microscopy
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in BLOC-2 complex genes (HPS3, HPS5, or HPS6)
History of bleeding diathesis including easy bruising, epistaxis, or prolonged bleeding after trauma
Evidence of progressive pulmonary fibrosis on imaging or pulmonary function testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of oculocutaneous albinism, platelet dense granule deficiency, and biallelic pathogenic variants in BLOC-2 genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm subtype and guide prognosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes pale skin, light hair, and iris transillumination
searchTerms: very light skin and hair color
lack of pigment in skin and eyes
pale skin and hair from pigment loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Platelet dense granule deficiency causing bleeding diathesis
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to easy bruising and prolonged bleeding
searchTerms: easy bleeding due to platelet defect

pathognomonic.symptomName: Biallelic mutations in BLOC-2 complex genes (HPS3, HPS5, HPS6)
searchTerms: inherited mutations causing pigment and bleeding issues
genetic defects in BLOC-2 complex genes
mutations causing platelet and pigmentation problems

common.notes: Light sensitivity common in affected individuals
searchTerms: light sensitivity from iris light shining through

common.notes: Involuntary eye movements often present from infancy

common.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after minor trauma or surgery
searchTerms: long bleeding after minor injuries or surgery
lung scarring with worsening shortness of breath
increasing difficulty breathing from lung damage
lung artery high pressure from scarring
high lung blood pressure due to lung disease

laboratory: Absent or markedly reduced platelet dense granules on electron microscopy
Normal platelet count with abnormal platelet function tests
imaging: High-resolution CT showing interstitial pulmonary fibrosis
Chest X-ray with reticulonodular infiltrates in lungs
other: Electron microscopy of platelets demonstrating absent dense bodies
Ophthalmologic exam showing iris transillumination and foveal hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in BLOC-3 complex genes (HPS1, HPS4)
Higher risk and earlier onset of pulmonary fibrosis

redFlags: Progressive dyspnea and hypoxia indicating pulmonary fibrosis
Severe bleeding episodes disproportionate to trauma
Granulomatous colitis causing severe gastrointestinal symptoms
